articles.title: ETFs Are Eating the World
articles.summary: The Wall Street Journal: ETFs Are Eating the World. Exchange-traded funds, which have existed for just 35 years, are booming at the expense of traditional mutual funds. More than 1,000 ETFs launched in the U.S. last year with the industry’s assets reaching $13.5 trillion, according to FactSet. A cumulative $3 trillion flowed out of traditional mutual funds between 2015 and 2024 with a similar sum moving to ETFs, according to the Investment Company Institute. Related tickers mentioned: CL=F, GS, TSM, TSMWF.

articles.title: BlackRock’s Profit Fell, Assets Hit Record $14 Trillion, in Fourth Quarter
articles.mainIdea: BlackRock’s Profit Fell, Assets Hit Record $14 Trillion, in Fourth Quarter
articles.summary: The Wall Street Journal: BlackRock’s Profit Fell, Assets Hit Record $14 Trillion, in Fourth Quarter. BlackRock’s profit fell in the fourth quarter on higher expenses, and the world’s largest money manager ended 2025 with more than $14 trillion in assets for the first time. BlackRock posted net income of $1.13 billion, down 33% from a year earlier. The stock market rebounded sharply from April, when fears about the effects of President Trump’s tariff plans sent the major indexes reeling, and ended 2025 near record highs. Related tickers mentioned: FDS.
